text:
lan: Heads-up — p95 host CPU spiked from ~16% -> ~31% on canary rollout (2.8.1). Noticed during traffic ramp.

anya: saw the alert. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/canary/5954330011 

tom: quick glance at flame: heavy time in host_tokenize + writev_copy + kv_lookup_hot.

zach: we shipped the writev->contiguous consolidation in proto_unwrap last week. could be copying more than before.

lan: did a perf run on a repro host. top stacks: 
```
proto_unwrap_copy_iovec()
host_tokenize_buf()
writev_coalesce()
memcpy
kv_cache_lookup_hot()
```

tom: kernel chooser also changed: shape-based model now picks kernel Z for tiny minibatches (<=2) because it had lower per-token cost in the microbench. But microbench didn't simulate fragmented streams.

anya: do we have KV hit-rate broken down by fragment_count or writev_fragments?

lan: pulled counts from canary logs: 
```
frag_count  avg_kv_hit  reqs
1          0.89        21k
2-3        0.55        12k
4+         0.34        6k
```

zach: wow — fragmentation clearly correlates with lower hit-rate. More fragments => more KV lookups and less amortization.

tom: hypothesis: kernel Z incurs an iovec->buf path for tokenizer (memcpy) per fragment which dominates for tiny fragments; kernel W avoids that by operating on iovec directly. Combined with fragmentation, Z loses badly.

anya: suggested mitigations?

lan: quick plan: 
- revert proto_unwrap consolidation in canary (fast rollback)
- enable a 2ms coalescer in front of host preparse to merge fragments from same conn
- tweak kernel chooser: prefer kernel W when effective_frag_count > 1 or effective_minibatch < 3
- add kv_prefetch(path) in kv_lookup to try preloading keys for next fragment

zach: low-risk changes: coalescer + kernel tweak. I'll author the coalescer toggle and a small metric tag frag_count.

tom: I'll add a kernel chooser flag and run local regressions. I can script loadgen to produce avg frag_count of 3.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2.8.1 started at 2026-03-21T14:02:00Z -> 25% (hosts: host-c2, host-d4)

lan: local run results (scripted fragmentation avg frag_count=3.2, 3k req/s, model latency stubbed to 150ms): 
- baseline (no consolidation, kernel W): p99 host cpu 18%
- consolidation on, kernel Z: p99 host cpu 36%
- consolidation off, coalescer on, kernel Z: p99 host cpu 22%
- consolidation off, coalescer on, kernel W + kv_prefetch: p99 host cpu 14%

anya: numbers look solid. coalescer buys a lot, but kernel W + prefetch is best.

zach: rolling canary rollback of consolidation now.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback to 2.8.0 (remove proto_unwrap consolidation) initiated at 2026-03-21T14:25:00Z -> 25%

lan: opened INF-987: "kernel-chooser: incorporate frag_count and prefer kernel W when frag_count>1 or minibatch<3". PR for coalescer and frag_count metric: https://phabricator/r/PR22334

tom: opened PR for kv_prefetch prototype (bench included): https://phabricator/r/PR22335

anya: monitoring KV hit by frag_count + p95/p99 host CPU. Will mute alerts until metrics stabilize. :white_check_mark:

lan: TL;DR: root cause = writev consolidation + kernel Z iovec->buf path + fragmented streams => KV thrash and memcpy hotpath. Fixes: rollback consolidation, add small coalescer, tweak kernel chooser, add kv_prefetch.

zach: will follow up with perf numbers after coalescer landed in canary.

lan: thanks all. we'll add note to postmortem if stable over 3h. :rocket:
